subject: Business Models
title: Data as Personal Property
description: A short lesson to help you apply Data as Personal Property.

hook.text: Your data generates $200/year for Google and Facebook combined. You get $0. Some want to change that.

buildup.text: Data ownership models propose that individuals should control and profit from their personal information.

discovery.text: Companies like Brave browser and Ocean Protocol pay users for their attention or data directly.

twist.text: GDPR gave Europeans data rights, but most click 'accept all cookies' anyway. Rights without behavior change little.

climax.text: If data ownership becomes law, the entire ad-tech industry—worth $600 billion—must restructure its business model.

punchline.text: $200/year of your data, $0 to you. Ownership could reshape a $600B industry.

quiz.question: What would happen if personal data ownership became standard?
options: The $600B ad-tech industry would need to restructure
